title: Momentum-resolved quantum noise spectroscopy using ensembles of diamond quantum sensors
authors: Zeeshawn Kazi, Kai-Hung Cheng, Jared Rovny, Nathalie P. de Leon
abstract: Spatiotemporal fluctuations across multiple scales govern and characterize the emergent properties, phase boundaries, and low-energy excitations of strongly correlated matter. However, capturing these dynamics has remained a major experimental challenge, as conventional probes typically offer either high spatial or temporal resolution, but not both simultaneously. Here, we leverage high-fidelity wide-field imaging of dense diamond nitrogen vacancy center ensembles to measure the momentum and frequency power spectral density of magnetic fluctuations. To access spatial wavevectors below the diffraction limit, we tune the sensing volume continuously through optical depletion. This approach enables study of equilibrium and driven fluctuations across three orders of magnitude in spatial scale and tunable frequency bands, providing a direct means to map low-energy, long-wavelength fluctuations in correlated systems.
summary: This paper details a technique using diamond NV centers to measure the momentum-resolved magnetic noise spectral density in correlated matter. By combining wide-field imaging with continuous tuning of the sensing volume, the authors overcome limitations in spatial and temporal resolution simultaneously. This allows for the direct mapping of low-energy, long-wavelength fluctuations crucial for understanding strongly correlated electronic phases.
main_problem: Characterizing spatiotemporal fluctuations across multiple scales in strongly correlated matter, which is difficult because conventional probes lack simultaneous high spatial and temporal resolution.
main_result: The developed technique allows mapping the full magnetic noise spectral density $S(\mathbf{q}, \omega)$ across tunable momentum and frequency bands, enabling the study of long-wavelength fluctuations.
method: The authors use high-fidelity wide-field imaging of diamond NV ensembles to measure momentum and frequency power spectral density of magnetic fluctuations, employing Fourier transforms of two-point correlation functions.
model_or_system: The physical system is a dense ensemble of nitrogen vacancy (NV) centers embedded in diamond. The measurement probes magnetic noise fluctuations, allowing access to momentum space ($\mathbf{q}$) and frequency ($\omega$) spectra.
key_observables: Momentum and frequency power spectral density of magnetic fluctuations, $S(\mathbf{q}, \omega_0)$; two-point magnetic field correlators $\langle B_{\omega_0}(\mathbf{x}_i)B_{\omega_0}(\mathbf{x}_j) angle$.
important_parameters: Spatial wavevectors ($\mathbf{q}$) spanning from $\mathbf{q}_{	ext{min}} \approx 2\pi 	imes 0.25 \mu	ext{m}^{-1}$ to $\mathbf{q}_{	ext{max}} \approx 2\pi 	imes 2 \mu	ext{m}^{-1}$; tunable frequency bands; sensing volume size ($D$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on relating the measured spectral density to the true spectrum via specific momentum filter functions derived for different geometries (wide-field vs. single-spot).
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the process of mapping magnetic field correlations and computing the Fourier transform to resolve features at finite momenta, and detail the wide-field spin-to-charge conversion readout.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops methods to measure the momentum-resolved spectral density $S(q, \omega)$ by relating it to measurable quantities (correlations, variances) using specific filter functions derived for different geometries (single center vs. ensemble vs. wide-field).
why_interesting: This work provides a novel, highly sensitive, and tunable experimental platform to measure dynamic correlations in condensed matter systems, bridging the gap between bulk measurements and nanoscale probing.
